- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model shows sharp upward spikes, cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overshoot.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 78–80), model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope.
- If model forecast starts rising sharply after a dip, check sentiment for bullish reversal — if sentiment is weak, adjust downward to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 2–5% to end of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows volatility spikes (e.g., 0.1–0.3) followed by model overreaction, apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility.
- When true outcome exceeds model by 5%+ in 3–5 consecutive days, model is underestimating trend — increase forecast by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
